status_note: A bug in the documentation, confirmed on 2.0.0 (Python, macOS arm64) against https://duckdb.org/docs/2.0/sql/functions/numeric.html; not filed. The engine's NaN is pinned by its own test (test/sql/types/float/ieee_floating_points.test#L23-L31), so the page is what is wrong.
summary: The documentation, not the engine: the numeric functions page (https://duckdb.org/docs/2.0/sql/functions/numeric.html, "Division and Modulo Operators") says "Integer division (`//`), modulo (`%`), and `INTERVAL / 0` throw an `Invalid Input Error` on division by zero instead of returning `NULL`." For FLOAT and DOUBLE, `%` by zero is NaN under the default `ieee_floating_point_ops`: `%` of floats binds `BindBinaryFloatingPoint<ModuloOperator>` (https://github.com/duckdb/duckdb/blob/v2.0.0/src/function/scalar/operator/arithmetic.cpp#L1452-L1469), which runs `std::fmod` without a zero check.

On the same page, the function `fmod` is documented as floored (true: `fmod(-7.5, 2)` is 0.5), while `%` on doubles is C's truncating `fmod` (`-7.5::DOUBLE % 2` is -1.5), and the page never says so: the C name and the operator behave oppositely without a word.
Suggested fix: "modulo (`%`) of integers and decimals", and a sentence that `%` on FLOAT and DOUBLE truncates (C's `fmod`) while the function `fmod` floors.
repro: `SELECT 1.0::DOUBLE % 0, 0.0::DOUBLE % 0, 1.0::FLOAT % 0` gives `nan, nan, nan`; `SELECT 1::INTEGER % 0` raises `Invalid Input Error`.
handling: No effect on sverify's results: its DuckDB SQL guards a zero divisor of `%` on doubles and writes NaN and ±inf out (duckdb-R15-double-modulus).
found_by: characterization pipeline reverse pass (#444): the docs read against duckdb-R15-double-modulus
